title: Fantasy Market and Strategy
description: Preserves source strategy, price sensitivity, timing, roster conditions and format dependence without converting it into a final Mighty Giants action.
principles: Preserve the source strategy and its preconditions.
Distinguish player evaluation from market value and action language.
Keep timing, liquidity, roster construction and format dependence.
Final Mighty Giants decisions require later league-specific analysis.

dimensions.description: Current market state, sentiment or positional environment.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve the market condition that makes the strategy relevant.
detection_questions: What market inefficiency or behavior is described?

dimensions.description: ADP, trade cost, pick range or waiver cost.
detection_questions: At what cost does the source action change?

dimensions.description: Buy, sell, hold, fade, stash, watch or trade-chip language.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve exact source intent and strength without turning it into a user recommendation.
detection_questions: What action label does the source use?

dimensions.description: When to act and what event changes timing.
detection_questions: Is the strategy preseason, in-season, before news or after injury?

dimensions.description: Team construction, contender status, handcuff ownership or need.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve the conditions under which the strategy applies.
detection_questions: Who should use this strategy and why?
Does league size, QB/TE setup, PPR or return scoring change the action?

dimensions.description: How easily the asset can be moved and to whom.
detection_questions: Is value concentrated with a specific manager or roster type?

dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve what the source prefers instead and why.
Retain downside, uncertainty and invalidating events.
detection_questions: What could make the strategy wrong?

passing: Preserve the reference only where it is needed to understand another argument.
Do not create an artificial standalone evaluation.
brief: Preserve the conclusion and its immediate qualifier or condition.
Do not expand beyond what the source supports.
substantive: Preserve the conclusion plus the meaningful reason, condition, risk or uncertainty supplied by the source.
Keep format, price or time-horizon distinctions when they materially change the view.
deep: Preserve the complete major reasoning chain rather than only the final verdict.
Represent every materially discussed dimension, including competing positive and negative cases.
Keep disagreements, uncertainty, conditions and failure paths.
structural: Preserve the broad thesis, its mechanism, its scope and the subjects it affects.
Create independently reusable context takes rather than burying the thesis inside one player.

review_questions: Is the source action tied to a price, timing and condition?
Is market value distinguished from player quality?
Are format and roster dependencies retained?
Has the extraction avoided converting source strategy into a final Mighty Giants recommendation?
forbidden_distortions: Do not omit price and present a conditional buy as an unconditional buy.
Do not turn market commentary into objective player truth.
Do not apply the strategy to Robert's roster during source extraction.
Do not remove timing or counterpart conditions.
extension_signals: A new market action or timing framework appears.
A salary, auction or contract-league mechanic needs its own profile.
A recurring liquidity or counterparty concept is missing.
The source introduces a new strategy segment type.
